chapter: Jeter-Pillars in Cleveland and St. Louis
title: St. Louis: Eddie Johnson's Crackerjacks and the Charlie Creath riverboat
summary: Edison names musicians around St. Louis, including Tab Smith, who later recommended him to Millinder, and the boat job.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Oh, we worked together around St. Louis a long time, Jo Jones and I. And Walter Page. And then a trumpet player, a tenor player, they added another tenor player to the band which is Gene Porter. He used to play with Earl Hines and then they had a band there who I just read in this book that they connected me with, Eddie Johnson and his Cracker Jacks. Harold Baker was playing with that band, see, and I never did play with the band. But I knew him quite well because they used to come through Columbus, Ohio. That's the first time I ever heard Tab Smith was with Eddie Johnson and Jacks his Cracker /, Tab Smith. That's the first time I heard him play.
Like when you were together with Lucky.
Yeah, right. And that's who recommended me for Lucky, you know. I had known Tab in St. Louis and he had left there before them but he used to come back.

Yes. They all used to play on the boat with Charlie Creath, you see. They played on the boat with Charlie Creath, which was the best job you could get in the season. And there was Sidney Catlett, he played on the boat, there was Louie Metcalf, Fate Marable, he was playing with Charlie Creath at the time. Later on he became a bandleader himself.
